Each active slice has at most \(r-1\) roots among the \(p\) Fourier characters by prime Fourier uncertainty. The sharpness constructions are explicit for every prime, including all admissible four-hole progression patterns. Central polynomial root product and side-row ratios force \(\alpha\beta=\gamma\delta\); converse construction proves completeness. Exhaustive exact cyclotomic verification of all three-point supports and all optimal progression hole patterns for \(p=5,7,11,13\) agrees. Risk: the numerical range of checks is finite; validity for all primes rests on the proof.

value.rationale: The matched three-tap constrained STFT is the first nontrivial support geometry beyond the separately known two-tap regime. A sharp gap of \(2p+2\) between progression and nonprogression minima, and the complete \(\alpha\beta=\gamma\delta\) zero-resonance classification, resolve natural questions of which time-frequency coefficients can vanish simultaneously. Exact optimal zero-pattern counts are structurally motivated by sparse-window signal localization rather than arbitrary finite slices. The result is an elementary but complete infinite-family classification; no broad sparse-recovery guarantees are claimed.
